correctness.rationale: For any field and rank-one nonzero operator N(X)=f(X)U on M_n(k), the associative Nijenhuis identity forces U²=λU. With c=f(U), the Nijenhuis identity equals weight-zero Rota–Baxter when c=0, and the rank-one RB equation itself forces c=0 by substituting X=U,Y=I. If c≠0 then ker f is a codimension-one subalgebra, so B_F(X,Y)=tr(FXY) vanishes on ker f×ker f; rank B_F≤2. Trace duality gives rank B_F=n rank(F), implying n=2 and rank(F)=1. Simplicity of M2 forces I∈ker f, so trF=0 and F²=0. Conjugate F to E12; the scalar identity is U²=(tr U)U and, by Cayley–Hamilton, det U=0, with c≠0 ensuring rank(U)=1. These and only these yield exceptional N with N²=cN. The projective generator count gives exceptional q²(q²−1), RB (q²−1)(2q+1), Nij (q²−1)(q+1)². Independently enumerated all 225 rank-one maps M2(F2)→M2(F2) by basis identities, obtaining RB=15, Nijenhuis=27, exceptional=12. Reviewed source GF2/3/4 verifier but did not substitute it for arbitrary-field proof. The identity proof works also in characteristic two.
